clue.text: The cob for a girl

definitions.meaning: a cob or cobnut is the nut of a common hedgerow tree

explanation.surface: Someone picks a cob as a present for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobnut grows on this tree, and it is also a traditional female first name.

clue.text: Drink following ball game

indicators.note: following places the drink after the word for ball in the answer

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance, a ball
Scotch is whisky, a drink

explanation.surface: A drink after a ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's game of hopping between squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Cross here — between a horse and a tiger?

definitions.meaning: a striped pedestrian crossing in Britain is named after this animal

definitions.text: between a horse and a tiger?
definitions.meaning: an animal shaped like a horse but striped like a tiger

explanation.surface: Asking where to cross between a horse and a tiger.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is the British black-and-white striped pedestrian crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped African equine gives its name to the British road crossing and looks like a striped horse.

clue.text: One's in no hurry to see it before king

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
taken as written
ere is an old word for before
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone leisurely watches events ahead of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dawdler or idler lingers aimlessly instead of hurrying.

clue.text: A letter said I would return payment for novel

indicators.note: return asks for the letters of the letter's spoken name and of I'D to be read backwards together

parts.note: the letter F, written as it is spoken, is EFF
I would contracts to I'D
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A letter-writer promises to send back the fee for a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses both opening pieces together, giving DIFFE. 'Novel' looks like a book but is the adjective, new.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means new and unlike anything before, i.e. unusual.

clue.text: Doctor takes very little money for intravenous administration

parts.note: 1p, one penny, written as if letters

explanation.surface: A doctor charges almost nothing for putting a patient on fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 is read as the letter I, so 1p, a single British penny, gives IP.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a device feeding fluid slowly into a vein.

clue.text: To get cheaper travel, he avoids paying

definitions.meaning: taking flights in the night hours, which are cheaper
a shady person who disappears to dodge debts

explanation.surface: Someone flies at night to save money and skips the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Night flights are cheaper; a fly-by-night is an unreliable person who slips away from obligations.

clue.text: Make use of unfinished polymer formation

indicators.note: formation suggests the letters are formed into a new arrangement
unfinished means the word polymer loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Putting a half-made plastic structure to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops R from POLYMER, leaving POLYME, which 'formation' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to use it.

clue.text: Profit from turning up the volume round the light unit

indicators.note: round means the reversed book goes around the unit
in a down clue turning up means the word for volume is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tome is a large book, a volume
the lumen is the SI unit of luminous flux

explanation.surface: Gain from cranking up the sound near the lighting department.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the book upwards as EMOT, which goes 'round' the unit of light.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary or fee, gain from employment.

clue.text: This is in leaf for a stated period

indicators.note: stated means the word is spoken, so its sound gives a differently spelt word

parts.note: time is a period

explanation.surface: Something appears in a leaf for a declared span.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a herb whose useful part is its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic herb is gathered for its small leaves.

clue.text: The bar permitted you to start with advertising

parts.note: a pub is a bar
licit means lawful, permitted

indicators.note: to start asks only for the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A pub landlord lets you open with some promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising and promotion both bring a product to public notice.

clue.text: Ask questions about neat agent

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the questioning word goes round the animal

parts.note: to pry is to ask nosy questions
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: Someone quizzes a tidy secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a deputy authorised to act for someone, as an agent does.

clue.text: Persuaded firm to cut down

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
axed means chopped or cut down

explanation.surface: A company was talked into making redundancies.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to win someone over by gentle urging.

clue.text: Cyrus, one resolved to be the centre of attraction

indicators.note: resolved read as re-solved, broken up and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: King Cyrus is determined to be the focus of everyone's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynosure is something that draws all eyes, a focal point of admiration.

clue.text: Blunder about providers of cheap accommodation in Bennett's book

indicators.note: about means the word for blunder goes around the hostel group

parts.note: a clanger is a blunder
YHA is the Youth Hostels Association, a British budget lodging network

explanation.surface: A mistake about cheap hostels in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Clayhanger is a 1910 novel by Arnold Bennett set in the Potteries.

clue.text: Offer to look in for meat

parts.note: to tender is to offer
lo is an old word meaning look
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bid to drop by for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prime cut of beef or pork from the loin.

clue.text: Unused to buying and selling and gambling on cards

parts.note: new means unused
a market is a place or system of buying and selling

explanation.surface: Someone new to trade and card betting.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is both an English horse-racing town and a card game played for stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a card game in which players bet chips on matching cards.

clue.text: Emblem of' Staffordshire town

definitions.meaning: the national vegetable badge of Wales
a market town in Staffordshire, an English county in the Midlands

explanation.surface: A Midlands town's coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is the Welsh national symbol, and it is also the name of a market town in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Committed a crime that's novel

definitions.meaning: a book by Robert Louis Stevenson

explanation.surface: A crime committed that is new.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct a person is a crime, and it is the title of Stevenson's 1886 adventure novel.

clue.text: Bloomers made by soccer players letting in the opposition finally

indicators.note: letting in means the footballers take a letter inside them

parts.note: kickers are players who kick, as in football

indicators.note: finally asks only for the closing letter of opposition

explanation.surface: Football players make mistakes letting in a late goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like blunders, but means underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers and knickers are both women's underpants.

clue.text: Get rid of a frog and a bird

definitions.meaning: to clear the throat noisily, a frog in the throat being hoarseness

explanation.surface: A frog is disposed of, and a bird appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear one's throat noisily is one sense; the other is a bird of prey such as a kestrel.

clue.text: Then he'd pay out, like 5

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Then he would settle up, like someone else did.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is the entry FLY-BY-NIGHT, written with dashes between its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-referenced answer is a compound joined by dashes between its words.

clue.text: Inward-turning scientist

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An introverted scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the naturalist behind the theory of evolution.

clue.text: Rough bit of water precedes a change of course, going astern

parts.note: a tear is a drop of water from the eye

indicators.note: going astern means moving backwards, so the word for the change of course is read in reverse

parts.note: to yaw is to swing off course

explanation.surface: Choppy water ahead of a ship that turns and reverses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astern' turns YAW into WAY. 'Rough' is the noun, a rowdy young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a hooligan, and a tearaway is a reckless, unruly youngster.

clue.text: Refuse to cut without due consideration

indicators.note: cut means the word to is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
rash means acting without due consideration

explanation.surface: Declining to make cuts carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks TO to T. 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household waste, rubbish.

clue.text: Bill sent to a US bureau. What'll they say …

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the United States

explanation.surface: An invoice goes to an American agency, and what will they make of it?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by sound: 'What'll', said aloud, is WATTLE, the Australian name for this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is the Australian common name for these thorny trees, so the spoken phrase points to them.

clue.text: Provide grub — but grub without support

indicators.note: without means the support word is taken away from the larva word

parts.note: a caterpillar is a grub, a larva
a pillar is a support

explanation.surface: Supplying food, but the food has no stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'grub' means a larva, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food for an event.

clue.text: This clue is blue

definitions.meaning: the clue sits in the list running vertically
feeling blue means low or sad

explanation.surface: This clue confesses to feeling sad.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a vertical-entry clue, and blue means low-spirited.

clue.text: … when gardens are not straight?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Kew Gardens is the famous botanic garden in south-west London

explanation.surface: Someone asks what happens when the garden beds are crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked, out of line.

clue.text: See post go out in March

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch the letter leave in the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is the verb, to walk in step.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose-step is a stiff-legged military way of marching.

clue.text: For such an accident, call coloured doctor, one from overseas

parts.note: hi is a call of greeting
tan means coloured brown, as by the sun
un is French for one

explanation.surface: After a crash, someone summons a dark-skinned foreign doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road crash where the driver leaves without stopping.

clue.text: She would pack a right in a scrap

indicators.note: pack means stuff something inside, so the contraction holds the letter for right

parts.note: she would contracts to SHE'D

explanation.surface: She would stuff a right-hand item into a scrap of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment.
